text: Why does optical fan-out to N synapses scale better than electronic fan-out in a neuromorphic system?
choices: Because optical fan-out charges N wire capacitors faster than electronics can
Because electronic fan-out is limited only by the speed of light
Because optics fans out by consuming more bandwidth per branch

Because electronic fan-out must charge N wire capacitances (RC- and energy-limited, worsening with N), while optics splits passively and WDM carries N channels on one waveguide, spending power (~P0/N per branch) rather than bandwidth
explanation: Electronic fan-out to N targets means driving N wire capacitances, an RC- and energy-limited operation that worsens with N; optically a single output splits passively and WDM lets one waveguide carry N wavelength channels, so fan-out costs optical power (~P0/N per branch) rather than bandwidth. Optics does not 'charge capacitors' (option 0) and it trades power, not bandwidth (option 2).
